questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A gland not associated with the alimentary canal is
questions.explanation:
The digestive glands associated with the alimentary canal are the salivary glands, liver and pancreas.
Their secretions (saliva, bile and pancreatic juice) are poured into the canal through ducts.
The adrenal gland is a ductless endocrine gland sitting on top of the kidney. It releases hormones into the blood, not into the gut.
The pancreas is tempting because it also has an endocrine part, but its exocrine part delivers pancreatic juice to the duodenum.
Answer: (2)
questions.credit: Source: NCERT Exemplar Biology Class 11, Ch 16 (MCQ Q4)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Statement I: Small amounts of glucose, amino acids and chloride ions are generally absorbed by simple diffusion.
Statement II: Simple diffusion of these substances into blood requires $Na^+$ carrier ions.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
questions.explanation:
Statement I is correct. NCERT says small amounts of monosaccharides like glucose, amino acids and some electrolytes like chloride ions are absorbed by simple diffusion.
Statement II is incorrect. Simple diffusion depends only on the concentration gradient.
The use of carrier ions such as $Na^+$ describes facilitated transport, not simple diffusion.
Answer: (4)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Statement I: Egestion of faeces is an involuntary process brought about entirely by local reflexes.
Statement II: The ileo-caecal valve prevents the backflow of faecal matter from the caecum into the ileum.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation:
Statement I is incorrect. The neural reflex from the rectum only creates the urge to defaecate.
Egestion itself is a voluntary process, carried out by mass peristaltic movement.
Statement II is correct. Undigested material enters the caecum through the ileo-caecal valve.
This valve prevents faecal matter from flowing back into the ileum.
Answer: (4)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 16 · Digestion and Absorption

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The mucosa of the stomach forms irregular folds. These folds are called:
questions.explanation:
The mucosa is the innermost layer of the gut wall, and it is folded differently in different regions.
In the stomach it forms irregular folds called rugae.
In the small intestine it forms finger-like folds called villi. Microvilli are projections of the cells lining the villi.
Crypts of Lieberkuhn lie between the bases of the intestinal villi.
Answer: (4)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 16 · Digestion and Absorption

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following is not a common disorder associated with digestive system?
questions.explanation:
NCERT lists jaundice, vomiting, diarrhoea, constipation and indigestion as digestive disorders. Dysentery is an intestinal infection.
Jaundice affects the liver and causes yellowing of skin and eyes due to bile pigments.
Diarrhoea means frequent watery stools. Dysentery means inflammation of the intestine with blood and mucus in the stools.
Tetanus is caused by the bacterium *Clostridium tetani* and affects the nervous system, causing muscle spasms. It is not a digestive disorder.
Answer: (1)
questions.credit: Source: NCERT Exemplar Biology Class 11, Ch 16 (MCQ Q3)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Statement I: Enzymatic digestion in the small intestine takes place in an alkaline medium of pH about 7.8.
Statement II: This alkaline medium is provided by mucus together with bicarbonates from the pancreas.
Choose the correct option.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
questions.explanation:
Statement I is correct. The intestinal medium is alkaline, at pH 7.8, which suits the action of pancreatic and intestinal enzymes.
Statement II is correct. Mucus from goblet cells and bicarbonates from the pancreas create this medium.
The same mucus and bicarbonates also protect the intestinal mucosa from acidic chyme.
Answer: (1)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Assertion (A): About 30% of dietary starch is hydrolysed in the buccal cavity itself.
Reason (R): The optimum pH of salivary amylase is 1.8.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true. Salivary amylase hydrolyses about 30% of starch to maltose in the oral cavity.
R is false. The optimum pH of salivary amylase is 6.8, which is nearly neutral.
pH 1.8 is the acidic pH of the stomach set up by HCl. It is optimal for pepsin.
The low pH of the stomach actually stops amylase from acting further.
Answer: (3)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Statement I: Fructose is absorbed from the small intestine with the help of carrier proteins (facilitated transport).
Statement II: Glucose is absorbed from the small intestine only by simple diffusion along its concentration gradient.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
questions.explanation:
Statement I is correct. Fructose and some amino acids are absorbed with carrier ions such as Na+, which is facilitated transport.
Statement II is incorrect. Glucose can enter by simple diffusion only in small amounts, depending on the concentration gradient. Most glucose, like other monosaccharides and amino acids, is absorbed by active transport against the gradient, using energy.
The word 'only' makes Statement II wrong.
Answer: (2)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about bile is correct?
options: It contains lipase, which hydrolyses fats into fatty acids and glycerol
It contains bile pigments, bile salts, cholesterol and phospholipids but no enzymes
It is synthesised by the gall bladder and released directly into the stomach
It reaches the duodenum only through the main pancreatic duct
questions.explanation:
(1) Incorrect: bile has no enzymes. It only activates lipases and emulsifies fats.
(2) Correct: bile contains bile pigments (bilirubin, biliverdin), bile salts, cholesterol and phospholipids.
(3) Incorrect: the liver makes bile. The gall bladder only stores and concentrates it. Bile goes to the duodenum, not the stomach.
(4) Incorrect: the bile duct and the pancreatic duct join to form the hepato-pancreatic duct, which opens into the duodenum.
Answer: (2)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which cells of the gastric glands secrete Castle's intrinsic factor, which is needed to absorb vitamin $B_{12}$?
questions.explanation:
Gastric glands have three major cell types: mucus neck cells, peptic (chief) cells and oxyntic (parietal) cells.
Oxyntic (parietal) cells secrete HCl and Castle's intrinsic factor, which is essential for absorbing vitamin $B_{12}$.
Chief cells secrete the proenzyme pepsinogen, not intrinsic factor.
Mucus neck cells secrete mucus.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 16 · Digestion and Absorption

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which region of the human small intestine is described in NCERT as the highly coiled part that opens into the large intestine?
questions.explanation:
NCERT divides the small intestine into three regions: the 'U' shaped duodenum, the long coiled middle jejunum and the highly coiled ileum.
The ileum is the last part, and it opens into the large intestine.
The jejunum is the most tempting wrong choice. It is coiled, but it is the middle region and does not open into the large intestine.
The caecum belongs to the large intestine, not the small intestine.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 16 · Digestion and Absorption

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Assertion (A): The pancreas is called a compound gland.
Reason (R): Its exocrine part secretes an alkaline pancreatic juice containing enzymes, and its endocrine part secretes the hormones insulin and glucagon.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true. NCERT describes the pancreas as a compound gland, meaning it is both exocrine and endocrine.
R is true. The exocrine part releases alkaline pancreatic juice rich in enzymes. The endocrine part releases insulin and glucagon.
Having both of these functions is exactly why the pancreas is called compound, so R correctly explains A.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 16 · Digestion and Absorption

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Lactase present in the succus entericus hydrolyses lactose into:
questions.explanation:
Disaccharidases in the intestinal juice act on specific disaccharides.
Lactose is broken down by lactase into glucose and galactose.
Maltose gives glucose + glucose through maltase.
Sucrose gives glucose + fructose through sucrase.
Answer: (3)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following statements are correct?
(i) The most highly coiled region of the small intestine is the jejunum.
(ii) The opening of the stomach into the duodenum is guarded by the pyloric sphincter.
(iii) In NCERT's description, the colon is divided into ascending, transverse and descending parts.
(iv) The rectum opens into the descending colon.
(v) The vermiform appendix is a vestigial organ.
questions.explanation:
(i) Incorrect: the ileum is highly coiled, while the jejunum is the long coiled middle part.
(ii) Correct: the pyloric sphincter guards the stomach-duodenum opening.
(iii) Correct: these are the three parts of the colon given by NCERT.
(iv) Incorrect: the descending colon opens into the rectum, not the other way round.
(v) Correct: the appendix is vestigial.
Correct statements: 3.
Answer: (2)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The sphincter of Oddi guards the opening of the
options: cystic duct into the gall bladder
common hepato-pancreatic duct into the duodenum
questions.explanation:
The bile duct and the pancreatic duct open together into the duodenum as the common hepato-pancreatic duct.
The sphincter of Oddi guards this common opening.
The opening of the stomach into the duodenum is guarded by the pyloric sphincter, not the sphincter of Oddi.
Answer: (3)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II and choose the correct option.
List-I
(a) Parotid gland
(b) Sub-mandibular gland
(c) Sub-lingual gland
(d) Glisson's capsule
List-II
(i) Lies below the tongue
(ii) Connective tissue sheath around each hepatic lobule
(iii) Located in the cheek region
(iv) Located in the region of the lower jaw
questions.explanation:
(a) The parotids are the salivary glands of the cheek region, so (a)-(iii).
(b) The sub-maxillary or sub-mandibular glands lie in the lower jaw region, so (b)-(iv).
(c) The sub-linguals lie below the tongue, so (c)-(i).
(d) Glisson's capsule is the thin connective tissue sheath that covers each hepatic lobule, so (d)-(ii).
Answer: (1)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match the two columns and select the right one among options given
Column I: A. Duodenum; B. Epiglottis; C. Glottis; D. Caecum
Column II: i. A cartilaginous flap; ii. Small blind sac; iii. ‘U’ shaped structure emerging from the stomach; iv. Opening of wind pipe
questions.explanation:
A–iii: the duodenum is the U-shaped first part of the small intestine, emerging from the stomach.
B–i: the epiglottis is a cartilaginous flap that covers the glottis during swallowing.
C–iv: the glottis is the opening of the windpipe (trachea).
D–ii: the caecum is a small blind sac at the start of the large intestine and bears the vermiform appendix.
This sequence (iii, i, iv, ii) matches option (3).
Answer: (3)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following correctly identifies the largest gland of the human body and its approximate weight in an adult?
questions.explanation:
The liver is the largest gland of the human body.
In an adult human it weighs about 1.2 to 1.5 kg.
The pancreas is a large compound gland, but it is much smaller than the liver.
A weight of 3.0–3.5 kg is far too high for the liver.
Answer: (2)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following are causes of indigestion?
(i) Inadequate enzyme secretion
(ii) Anxiety
(iii) Food poisoning
(iv) Overeating
(v) Spicy food
(vi) Deposition of bile pigments in skin
questions.explanation:
(i) to (v) Correct: NCERT lists inadequate enzyme secretion, anxiety, food poisoning, overeating and spicy food as causes of indigestion.
Indigestion means food is not properly digested, which leads to a feeling of fullness.
(vi) Incorrect: deposition of bile pigments in the skin is a feature of jaundice, not a cause of indigestion.
So five items are causes.
Answer: (3)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The approximate pH of human saliva is
questions.explanation:
Saliva is a nearly neutral, slightly acidic fluid with a pH of about 6.8.
It also carries electrolytes ($Na^+$, $K^+$, $Cl^-$, $HCO_3^-$) and enzymes such as salivary amylase and lysozyme.
pH 1.8 is the pH of the stomach contents, produced by HCl, so it is the most tempting wrong choice.
pH values of 7.8 and 8.6 are alkaline. Saliva is not alkaline.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 16 · Digestion and Absorption

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following statements about the human buccal cavity are correct?
(i) The upper surface of the tongue bears small projections called papillae, some of which bear taste buds.
(ii) Every papilla on the tongue carries taste buds.
(iii) The hard chewing surface of teeth is made of enamel and helps in mastication.
(iv) The dental formula shows the arrangement of teeth in each half of the upper and lower jaw in the order I, C, PM, M.
(v) Each half of the adult human jaw has three premolars.
questions.explanation:
(i) Correct: papillae are present on the upper surface of the tongue, and some of them bear taste buds.
(ii) Incorrect: only some papillae bear taste buds, not all.
(iii) Correct: enamel forms the hard chewing surface.
(iv) Correct: the dental formula is written for each half-jaw in the order I, C, PM, M.
(v) Incorrect: the formula 2123 shows 2 premolars per half-jaw; it is the molars that number 3.
Three statements are correct.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 16 · Digestion and Absorption

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following statements about regulation of gastrointestinal activity are correct?
(i) Muscular activities of the alimentary canal can be moderated by neural mechanisms, both local and through the CNS.
(ii) Hormonal control of digestive juice secretion is carried out by local hormones produced by the gastric and intestinal mucosa.
(iii) Gastric and intestinal secretions are controlled only by hormones and never by neural signals.
(iv) Gastric inhibitory peptide stimulates gastric secretion and motility.
(v) Secretin stimulates the release of water and bicarbonate ions from the pancreas.
questions.explanation:
(i) Correct: gut muscle activity is moderated by local neural mechanisms and by the CNS.
(ii) Correct: digestive juice secretion is controlled by local hormones from the gastric and intestinal mucosa.
(iii) Incorrect: gastric and intestinal secretions are also stimulated by neural signals.
(iv) Incorrect: GIP inhibits gastric secretion and motility.
(v) Correct: secretin releases water and bicarbonate ions from the exocrine pancreas.
Three statements are correct.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 16 · Digestion and Absorption

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A labelled diagram of the hepato-pancreatic complex shows the following. Duct P arises from a thin muscular sac. Duct Q arises from the largest gland of the body. P and Q unite to form duct X. Duct X then joins duct Y, which comes from an elongated gland lying in the loop of the duodenum. The combined duct opens into the duodenum through an opening guarded by a ring of muscle Z. Identify X and Z.
options: X = cystic duct; Z = pyloric sphincter
X = common bile duct; Z = sphincter of Oddi
X = hepato-pancreatic duct; Z = sphincter of Oddi
X = common bile duct; Z = pyloric sphincter
questions.explanation:
P is the cystic duct, which comes from the gall bladder (the thin muscular sac).
Q is the hepatic duct, which comes from the liver (the largest gland).
The union of P and Q forms X, the common bile duct.
X joins Y, the pancreatic duct, to form the common hepato-pancreatic duct.
This duct opens into the duodenum, and its opening is guarded by Z, the sphincter of Oddi.
The pyloric sphincter guards the stomach's opening into the duodenum instead, so options (1) and (4) are wrong.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 16 · Digestion and Absorption

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which sequence correctly lists the layers of the wall of the small intestine, starting from the lumen and moving outward?
questions.explanation:
The mucosa lines the lumen, so it is the innermost layer.
The submucosa lies just outside it and is made of loose connective tissue with nerves and vessels.
Next is the muscularis, the smooth muscle layer.
The serosa is the outermost layer.
Option (1) is the same order read from outside to inside. Option (2) wrongly places the muscularis before the submucosa.
Answer: (3)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Statement I: Food leaving the stomach passes through the duodenum, jejunum and ileum, in that order, before entering the caecum.
Statement II: The descending colon opens directly to the exterior through the anus.
Choose the correct option.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation:
Statement I is correct. The small intestine runs duodenum → jejunum → ileum, and the ileum opens into the caecum.
Statement II is incorrect. The descending colon opens into the rectum, and the rectum opens out through the anus.
Answer: (3)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Assertion (A): Absorption of glucose and $Na^+$ by active transport requires energy.
Reason (R): Active transport moves substances against their concentration gradient.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true. NCERT lists amino acids, glucose and $Na^+$ among the nutrients absorbed by active transport, which needs energy.
R is true. Active transport works against the concentration gradient.
Moving a substance against its gradient is exactly why energy is needed, so R correctly explains A.
Answer: (1)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In constipation, faeces are retained within the
questions.explanation:
NCERT: in constipation, the faeces are retained within the rectum because bowel movements occur irregularly.
The caecum and ileum lie before the colon and do not store faeces.
The colon carries undigested matter forward to the rectum, where faeces are stored before defaecation.
Answer: (3)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List-I (gland) with List-II (location):
List-I
A. Parotid gland
B. Sublingual gland
C. Brunner's glands
D. Crypts of Lieberkuhn
List-II
(i) Submucosa of the duodenum
(ii) Cheek region
(iii) Mucosa, at the bases between villi of the intestine
(iv) Below the tongue
questions.explanation:
A: Parotid glands lie in the cheek region, so A-(ii).
B: Sublingual glands lie below the tongue, so B-(iv).
C: Brunner's glands lie in the submucosa of the duodenum, so C-(i).
D: Crypts of Lieberkuhn are tubular glands of the mucosa, found at the bases between the villi, so D-(iii).
Option (3) swaps Brunner's glands and the crypts. Brunner's glands are submucosal, not mucosal.
Answer: (1)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Assertion (A): Chymotrypsinogen and procarboxypeptidases of pancreatic juice become active only after reaching the intestinal lumen.
Reason (R): Trypsin, formed from trypsinogen by the action of enterokinase, activates the other enzymes of pancreatic juice.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true. These proteolytic enzymes are secreted in inactive form and work only in the intestine.
R is true. Enterokinase from the intestinal mucosa converts trypsinogen into trypsin, and trypsin then activates the other pancreatic enzymes.
Enterokinase is available only in the intestine, so this activation chain starts only there. R therefore correctly explains A.
Answer: (1)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In humans, each tooth is fixed in a socket of the jaw bone. This type of attachment is called
questions.explanation:
Thecodont means each tooth sits in a bony socket of the jaw, which is the human condition.
Heterodont refers to teeth of different types, not to how they are attached.
Diphyodont refers to two sets of teeth in a lifetime.
Acrodont teeth are fused to the jaw surface without sockets, so this is not the human condition.
Answer: (3)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which structure prevents food from entering the glottis during swallowing?
questions.explanation:
The glottis is the opening of the wind pipe (trachea).
The epiglottis is a cartilaginous flap that closes over the glottis during swallowing, so food goes into the oesophagus.
The sphincters lie further down the gut and do not guard the airway.
Answer: (2)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which one of the following statements about digestion in the stomach is correct?
options: Food stays in the stomach for about 1 hour, and the churned food is called bolus
Pepsin converts proteins directly into free amino acids
Mucus and bicarbonates in gastric juice protect the mucosal epithelium from concentrated HCl
Chief cells secrete HCl, which provides a pH of about 6.8
questions.explanation:
(1) Incorrect. Food is stored for 4–5 hours, and the churned, acidic food is called chyme, not bolus.
(2) Incorrect. Pepsin converts proteins into proteoses and peptones, not into free amino acids.
(3) Correct. Mucus and bicarbonates lubricate the mucosal epithelium and protect it from excoriation by concentrated HCl.
(4) Incorrect. HCl comes from the oxyntic cells and gives a pH of about 1.8.
Answer: (3)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Assertion (A): Salivary secretion can begin even before food is placed in the mouth.
Reason (R): The sight and smell of food can stimulate salivary secretion through neural signals.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true: saliva often starts flowing before food reaches the oral cavity.
R is true: NCERT states that the sight, smell and/or presence of food in the oral cavity can stimulate saliva secretion through neural control.
Because the sight and smell of food act before the food is eaten, R directly explains A.
Answer: (1)

questions.question: The hard chewing surface of teeth that helps in mastication of food is made up of
questions.explanation:
NCERT states that the hard chewing surface of the teeth is made up of enamel and that it helps in mastication.
Dentine lies beneath the enamel.
Cementum covers the root.
Pulp is the soft inner core containing nerves and blood vessels.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The tongue is attached to the floor of the oral cavity by a fold called the
questions.explanation:
NCERT describes the tongue as a freely movable muscular organ. It is attached to the floor of the oral cavity by the frenulum.
Papillae are small projections on the upper surface of the tongue and do not attach it.
The epiglottis is a cartilaginous flap that guards the glottis.
The uvula hangs from the soft palate.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Statement I: In jaundice, the skin and eyes turn yellow due to deposition of bile pigments such as bilirubin.
Statement II: Bile pigments are secreted by the gall bladder, so jaundice is primarily a disorder of the gall bladder.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
questions.explanation:
Statement I is correct: bile contains the pigments bilirubin and biliverdin. In jaundice, their deposition in the skin and eyes makes them yellow.
Statement II is incorrect: bile, including its pigments, is secreted by hepatic cells of the liver. The gall bladder only stores and concentrates it.
NCERT states that the liver is the organ affected in jaundice.
Answer: (2)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following statements are correct?
(i) The liver lies in the abdominal cavity just below the diaphragm and has two lobes.
(ii) The gall bladder secretes bile.
(iii) The common hepato-pancreatic duct is guarded by the sphincter of Oddi.
(iv) The pancreas lies between the limbs of the 'U' shaped duodenum.
(v) The sub-lingual salivary glands are located in the cheeks.
questions.explanation:
(i) Correct: the liver lies just below the diaphragm and has two lobes.
(ii) Incorrect: bile is secreted by the hepatic cells. The gall bladder only stores and concentrates it.
(iii) Correct: the sphincter of Oddi guards the hepato-pancreatic duct.
(iv) Correct: the pancreas lies between the limbs of the U-shaped duodenum.
(v) Incorrect: the sub-linguals lie below the tongue. The parotids are the cheek glands.
Three statements are correct.
Answer: (2)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List-I (enzyme) with List-II (product formed) and choose the correct option.
List-I:
A. Pepsin
B. Nucleosidases
C. Pancreatic lipase
D. Salivary amylase
List-II:
i. Maltose
ii. Sugars and bases
iii. Proteoses and peptones
iv. Di- and monoglycerides
questions.explanation:
A-iii: Pepsin converts proteins into proteoses and peptones in the stomach.
B-ii: Nucleosidases break nucleosides into sugars and bases. This is the last step after nucleases and nucleotidases.
C-iv: Lipase breaks emulsified fats (triglycerides) into di- and monoglycerides.
D-i: Salivary amylase hydrolyses starch into the disaccharide maltose.
Answer: (4)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 16 · Digestion and Absorption

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which one of the following pairs of a gastric gland cell type and its secretion is correctly matched?
options: Chief (peptic) cells – HCl and intrinsic factor
Parietal (oxyntic) cells – HCl and intrinsic factor
questions.explanation:
Gastric glands have three major cell types.
Mucus neck cells secrete mucus.
Chief or peptic cells secrete the proenzyme pepsinogen.
Parietal or oxyntic cells secrete HCl and intrinsic factor, the factor needed for absorption of vitamin $B_{12}$.
Option (1) gives the parietal cell secretions to chief cells, and option (2) gives the chief cell secretion to mucus cells. Goblet cells secrete mucus, not rennin.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 16 · Digestion and Absorption

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following statements about the wall of the human alimentary canal are correct?
(i) The serosa, the outermost layer, is made of a thin mesothelium with some connective tissue.
(ii) The muscularis usually has an inner circular and an outer longitudinal layer of smooth muscle.
(iii) The villi of the small intestine are projections of the submucosa.
(iv) In the stomach, the mucosa forms irregular folds called rugae.
(v) Crypts of Lieberkuhn are present between the bases of the villi.
questions.explanation:
(i) Correct: the serosa is a thin mesothelium (visceral organ epithelium) with some connective tissue.
(ii) Correct: the muscularis has inner circular and outer longitudinal muscle, with an oblique layer in some regions.
(iii) Incorrect: villi are small finger-like folds of the mucosa, not the submucosa.
(iv) Correct: the gastric mucosa forms rugae.
(v) Correct: the crypts of Lieberkuhn are glands lying between the bases of the villi.
So 4 statements are correct.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 16 · Digestion and Absorption

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The mucus secreted in the large intestine mainly helps to
options: digest the remaining starch in the undigested food
neutralise the acidic chyme coming from the stomach
hold waste particles together and lubricate them for easy passage
questions.explanation:
NCERT says the mucus of the large intestine adheres the undigested waste particles together.
It also lubricates them so that they pass easily towards the rectum.
Mucus contains no starch-digesting enzyme.
Chyme is neutralised in the duodenum by bile, pancreatic juice and intestinal secretions, not by colonic mucus.
Trypsinogen is activated by enterokinase in the small intestine.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 16 · Digestion and Absorption

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Assertion (A): The mucosa of the small intestine forms small finger-like foldings called villi.
Reason (R): Villi are outgrowths of the sub-mucosa that are covered on their surface by the serosa.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true. In the small intestine, the mucosa forms small finger-like foldings called villi.
R is false. Villi are foldings of the mucosa, not of the sub-mucosa.
The serosa is the outermost layer of the gut wall, facing the body cavity. It does not cover the villi, which project into the lumen.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 16 · Digestion and Absorption

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a function of the human large intestine?
options: Absorption of some water and minerals
Secretion of mucus that holds waste particles together and lubricates their passage
Enzymatic breakdown of peptides into amino acids
questions.explanation:
No significant digestive activity occurs in the large intestine, according to NCERT.
Its functions are absorbing some water, minerals and certain drugs. It also secretes mucus, which binds undigested waste particles together and lubricates them for easy passage, so options (1), (2) and (3) are true functions.
Protein digestion into amino acids is finished by intestinal and pancreatic enzymes in the small intestine, not the colon. So option (4) is not a function of the large intestine.
Answer: (4)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 16 · Digestion and Absorption

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II.
List-I
(A) Duodenum
(B) Jejunum
(C) Ileum
(D) Caecum
List-II
(i) Highly coiled part that opens into the large intestine
(ii) Blind sac hosting symbiotic micro-organisms
(iii) 'U'-shaped first part of the small intestine
(iv) Long coiled middle portion of the small intestine
Choose the correct option.
questions.explanation:
(A) Duodenum: the 'U'-shaped first part, so (iii).
(B) Jejunum: the long coiled middle portion, so (iv).
(C) Ileum: the highly coiled part that opens into the large intestine, so (i).
(D) Caecum: the small blind sac with symbiotic micro-organisms, so (ii).
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 16 · Digestion and Absorption

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Arrange the following structures in the order in which food passes through them after leaving the stomach:
(i) Ascending colon
(ii) Jejunum
(iii) Ileo-caecal valve
(iv) Transverse colon
(v) Pyloric sphincter
(vi) Caecum
questions.explanation:
Food leaves the stomach through the pyloric sphincter (v) and enters the duodenum, then the jejunum (ii), then the ileum.
The ileum opens into the large intestine at the ileo-caecal valve (iii), and food enters the caecum (vi).
The caecum opens into the colon, which runs ascending (i), then transverse (iv), then descending, before reaching the rectum.
Option (1) is wrong because it places the caecum before the valve.
Option (3) is wrong because it reverses the order of the colon parts.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 16 · Digestion and Absorption

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Complete digestion of nucleic acids in the small intestine requires three enzymes acting one after another. Which option gives the correct sequence along with the juice that supplies each enzyme?
options: Nucleotidases (pancreatic juice) → Nucleases (intestinal juice) → Nucleosidases (intestinal juice)
Nucleases (pancreatic juice) → Nucleosidases (intestinal juice) → Nucleotidases (intestinal juice)
Nucleases (pancreatic juice) → Nucleotidases (intestinal juice) → Nucleosidases (intestinal juice)
Nucleases (intestinal juice) → Nucleotidases (pancreatic juice) → Nucleosidases (pancreatic juice)
questions.explanation:
Nucleases of pancreatic juice break nucleic acids into nucleotides.
Nucleotidases of intestinal juice then convert nucleotides into nucleosides.
Nucleosidases of intestinal juice finally split nucleosides into sugars and bases.
Option (2) swaps the last two steps. Nucleosidase cannot act until nucleosides have been formed.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 16 · Digestion and Absorption

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Hepato-pancreatic duct opens into the duodenum and carries
questions.explanation:
The bile duct from the liver and gall bladder joins the pancreatic duct. Together they form the common hepato-pancreatic duct.
This duct opens into the duodenum, and its opening is guarded by the sphincter of Oddi.
It therefore carries both bile and pancreatic juice. Options (1) and (2) are each only half the answer.
Saliva enters the buccal cavity, not the duodenum.
Answer: (3)
questions.credit: Source: NCERT Exemplar Biology Class 11, Ch 16 (MCQ Q2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 16 · Digestion and Absorption

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List-I (part of alimentary canal) with List-II (absorption occurring there):
List-I
A. Mouth
B. Stomach
C. Small intestine
D. Large intestine
List-II
i. Principal organ of absorption, including fatty acids and glycerol (as micelles)
ii. Water, simple sugars and alcohol
iii. Water, some minerals and drugs
iv. Certain drugs in contact with the mucosa of the mouth and lower side of the tongue
questions.explanation:
A–iv: In the mouth, certain drugs that touch the mucosa and the lower side of the tongue enter the blood capillaries.
B–ii: The stomach absorbs water, simple sugars and alcohol.
C–i: The small intestine is the principal organ of absorption. Fatty acids and glycerol enter it as micelles.
D–iii: The large intestine absorbs water, some minerals and drugs.
Option (1) wrongly gives the large intestine's absorption to the stomach.
Answer: (4)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 16 · Digestion and Absorption

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II.
List-I
(A) Lysozyme
(B) Rennin
(C) HCl
(D) Pepsin
List-II
(i) Converts proteins into proteoses and peptones
(ii) Antibacterial agent in saliva
(iii) Proteolytic enzyme that helps digest milk proteins in infants
(iv) Activates pepsinogen and maintains pH of about 1.8
Choose the correct option.
questions.explanation:
(A) Lysozyme is present in saliva. It acts as an antibacterial agent and prevents infections, so A-(ii).
(B) Rennin is a proteolytic enzyme in the gastric juice of infants that helps digest milk proteins, so B-(iii).
(C) HCl converts pepsinogen to pepsin and provides an acidic pH of about 1.8, so C-(iv).
(D) Pepsin converts proteins into proteoses and peptones, so D-(i).
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 16 · Digestion and Absorption

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about human teeth is incorrect?
options: Each tooth is fixed in a socket of the jaw bone (thecodont attachment)
Humans form two sets of teeth during life (diphyodont condition)
An adult has 32 permanent teeth of four different types
Each half of the upper jaw of an adult has three premolars
questions.explanation:
The dental formula $\frac{2123}{2123}$ gives the teeth in each half of the upper and lower jaw: 2 incisors, 1 canine, 2 premolars and 3 molars. So each half-jaw has two premolars, not three, and option (4) is incorrect.
The thecodont, diphyodont and heterodont descriptions in the other options are correct.
The four teeth types total 32 permanent teeth.
Answer: (4)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 16 · Digestion and Absorption

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Assertion (A): The ileo-caecal valve, at the junction of the small and large intestine, prevents contents of the large intestine from flowing back into the small intestine.
Reason (R): The ileum opens directly into the rectum.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true. The ileo-caecal valve guards the opening of the ileum into the caecum and stops backflow into the ileum.
R is false. The ileum opens into the caecum, the first part of the large intestine.
The rectum receives material from the descending colon, not from the ileum.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 16 · Digestion and Absorption

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The absorbed end products of digestion reach the body tissues, which use them for their activities. According to NCERT, what is this process called?
questions.explanation:
Absorption is the passage of digestion end products through the intestinal mucosa into blood or lymph.
When these absorbed substances reach the tissues and are used for their activities, the process is called assimilation.
Absorption is the tempting wrong option, but it only covers entry into blood or lymph, not use by the tissues.
Egestion is the removal of faeces. Emulsification is the breaking of fats into small droplets by bile.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 16 · Digestion and Absorption

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
An undigested plant fibre travels from the small intestine to the exterior. Arrange the structures it passes through in the correct sequence:
(i) Transverse colon
(ii) Caecum
(iii) Rectum
(iv) Ileum
(v) Descending colon
(vi) Ascending colon
questions.explanation:
The ileum, the last part of the small intestine, opens into the caecum.
The caecum opens into the colon. Material moves through its ascending part first, then the transverse part, then the descending part.
The descending colon opens into the rectum, which opens out through the anus.
Sequence: ileum → caecum → ascending → transverse → descending colon → rectum.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 16 · Digestion and Absorption

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II.
List-I
A. Rugae
B. Lacteal
C. Crypts of Lieberkuhn
D. Brunner's glands
List-II
i. Large lymph vessel present in each villus
ii. Glands located in the sub-mucosa of the duodenum
iii. Irregular folds of the mucosa of the stomach
iv. Mucosal pits lying in between the bases of the villi
questions.explanation:
A-iii: rugae are irregular folds of the mucosa of the stomach.
B-i: the lacteal is a large lymph vessel inside each villus. It takes up fat-derived products.
C-iv: crypts of Lieberkuhn are formed by the mucosa between the bases of the villi.
D-ii: Brunner's glands are sub-mucosal glands of the duodenum. Their secretion helps protect the mucosa from acid.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 16 · Digestion and Absorption

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Arrange the following events of fat absorption in the correct sequence:
(i) Chylomicrons enter the lacteals
(ii) Fatty acids and glycerol are incorporated into micelles
(iii) Lymph vessels release the absorbed substances into the blood stream
(iv) Fats are re-formed into protein-coated fat globules inside the intestinal mucosa
(v) Micelles move into the intestinal mucosa
questions.explanation:
Fatty acids and glycerol are insoluble, so they first form micelles (ii).
The micelles move into the intestinal mucosa (v).
Inside the mucosa, the fats are re-formed into protein-coated chylomicrons (iv).
The chylomicrons enter the lacteals of the villi (i).
The lymph vessels finally empty these substances into the blood stream (iii).
Answer: (4)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 16 · Digestion and Absorption

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The reflex ejection of stomach contents through the mouth is controlled by a centre located in the
questions.explanation:
Vomiting is the ejection of stomach contents through the mouth.
It is a reflex action controlled by the vomit centre in the medulla (medulla oblongata).
The hypothalamus regulates hunger and thirst, not the vomiting reflex.
The cerebellum and cerebrum are not reflex centres for vomiting.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 16 · Digestion and Absorption

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A dentist numbers the teeth in the upper right quadrant of an adult's mouth from 1 to 8, starting at the midline and moving backwards. The teeth numbered 3 and 6 would respectively be
questions.explanation:
The dental formula $\frac{2123}{2123}$ gives the order in one half jaw as I, C, PM, M.
Counting from the midline: 1, 2 = incisors; 3 = canine; 4, 5 = premolars; 6, 7, 8 = molars.
So tooth 3 is the canine and tooth 6 is the first molar.
Option (3) fails because there are two premolars before the molars, so position 6 is already a molar.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 16 · Digestion and Absorption

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following gives the correct path followed by bile from its site of formation until it enters the duodenum, when it is stored before release?
options: Gall bladder → hepatic duct → cystic duct → common bile duct → hepato-pancreatic duct → duodenum
Hepatic cells → hepatic duct → gall bladder → cystic duct → common bile duct → hepato-pancreatic duct → duodenum
Hepatic cells → cystic duct → hepatic duct → gall bladder → pancreatic duct → duodenum
Hepatic cells → common bile duct → gall bladder → hepatic duct → hepato-pancreatic duct → duodenum
questions.explanation:
Bile is secreted by the hepatic cells and leaves the liver through the hepatic ducts.
It is stored and concentrated in the gall bladder.
It leaves the gall bladder through the cystic duct.
The cystic duct joins the hepatic duct to form the common bile duct.
The common bile duct joins the pancreatic duct as the hepato-pancreatic duct, which opens into the duodenum.
The gall bladder only stores bile and does not make it, so option (1) is wrong.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 16 · Digestion and Absorption

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II.
List-I
A. Thecodont
B. Diphyodont
C. Heterodont
D. Enamel
List-II
i. Different types of teeth present
ii. Hard chewing surface of teeth
iii. Teeth embedded in sockets of jaw bones
iv. Two sets of teeth formed during life
questions.explanation:
A-iii: In the thecodont condition, each tooth sits in a jaw-bone socket.
B-iv: Diphyodont means two sets of teeth form during life, milk teeth followed by permanent teeth.
C-i: Heterodont means different tooth types are present (I, C, PM, M).
D-ii: Enamel forms the hard chewing surface that helps in mastication.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 16 · Digestion and Absorption

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The dental formula of an adult human is $\frac{2123}{2123}$. Using this formula, which option correctly gives the total number of teeth in the upper jaw and the total number of molars in the entire mouth?
questions.explanation:
The formula gives the teeth in one half of each jaw. The order is I = 2, C = 1, PM = 2, M = 3, so one half-jaw has 8 teeth.
The upper jaw has two halves, so it has 2 × 8 = 16 teeth.
There are 3 molars per half-jaw and four half-jaws in the mouth, giving 3 × 4 = 12 molars.
Check: 16 upper + 16 lower = 32 permanent teeth.
Option (1) counts only one half-jaw (8 teeth). Option (3) counts molars in only one jaw (6).
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 16 · Digestion and Absorption

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List-I (enzyme of succus entericus) with List-II (products formed):
List-I
A. Maltase
B. Sucrase
C. Dipeptidases
D. Nucleosidases
List-II
i. Amino acids
ii. Sugars + bases
iii. Glucose + Glucose
iv. Glucose + Fructose
questions.explanation:
A. Maltase acts on maltose to give glucose + glucose (iii).
B. Sucrase acts on sucrose to give glucose + fructose (iv).
C. Dipeptidases act on dipeptides to give amino acids (i).
D. Nucleosidases act on nucleosides to give sugars + bases (ii).
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 16 · Digestion and Absorption

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following are normal components of human saliva?
$Na^+$, $K^+$, $Cl^-$, $HCO_3^-$, salivary amylase, lysozyme, pepsinogen, HCl
questions.explanation:
Saliva contains the electrolytes $Na^+$, $K^+$, $Cl^-$ and $HCO_3^-$. That gives 4.
It also contains two enzymes, salivary amylase and lysozyme. That gives 2 more.
Pepsinogen comes from the chief cells of the stomach, not from the salivary glands.
HCl comes from the oxyntic cells of the stomach, not from the salivary glands.
The total is therefore 6.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 16 · Digestion and Absorption

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following does NCERT list as being absorbed into blood by active transport?
Amino acids, glucose, $Na^+$, water, fatty acids, glycerol
questions.explanation:
Amino acids, glucose and $Na^+$ are absorbed by active transport. That makes 3.
Water is not counted, because it moves along the osmotic gradient.
Fatty acids and glycerol are not counted either. They are insoluble, so they are taken up through micelles and leave as chylomicrons into lymph.
Total = 3.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 16 · Digestion and Absorption

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Statement I: The oesophagus is a thin, long tube that passes through the neck, thorax and diaphragm before reaching the stomach.
Statement II: The oesophagus opens into the pyloric portion of the stomach.
Choose the correct option.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation:
Statement I is correct. The oesophagus extends posteriorly through the neck, thorax and diaphragm and leads to the stomach.
Statement II is incorrect. The oesophagus opens into the cardiac portion of the stomach.
The pyloric portion lies at the other end and opens into the duodenum.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 16 · Digestion and Absorption

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following correctly traces the path of bile that is first stored in the gall bladder and later released into the duodenum?
options: Hepatic cells → cystic duct → gall bladder → hepatic duct → common bile duct → duodenum
Hepatic cells → hepatic duct → common bile duct → gall bladder → cystic duct → duodenum
Hepatic cells → gall bladder → hepatic duct → hepato-pancreatic duct → common bile duct → duodenum
Hepatic cells → hepatic duct → gall bladder → cystic duct → common bile duct → hepato-pancreatic duct → duodenum
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Bile is secreted by the hepatic cells and leaves the liver through the hepatic ducts.
Step 2: It is stored and concentrated in the gall bladder.
Step 3: The duct of the gall bladder (cystic duct) joins the hepatic duct to form the common bile duct.
Step 4: The common bile duct joins the pancreatic duct to form the hepato-pancreatic duct. This duct opens into the duodenum and is guarded by the sphincter of Oddi.
Only option 4 follows this order.
Answer: (4)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 16 · Digestion and Absorption

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Using the human dental formula $\frac{2123}{2123}$, what is the total number of premolars in an adult human?
questions.explanation:
The formula gives the teeth in one half of each jaw in the order I, C, PM, M.
Premolars per half jaw = 2.
There are 4 half jaws (upper left, upper right, lower left, lower right).
Total premolars = 2 × 4 = 8.
The option 12 is the total for molars, not premolars.
Answer: (4)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 16 · Digestion and Absorption

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A person has a hereditary inability to secrete enterokinase, while all other digestive secretions are normal. Which process would be most directly impaired?
options: Emulsification of fats into micelles in the duodenum
Conversion of proteins, proteoses and peptones into dipeptides in the small intestine
Hydrolysis of maltose into glucose by intestinal juice
Partial digestion of proteins by pepsin in the stomach
questions.explanation:
Without enterokinase, trypsinogen cannot be converted into trypsin.
Trypsin is needed to activate the other pancreatic enzymes, including chymotrypsinogen and procarboxypeptidases.
These enzymes convert proteins, proteoses and peptones into dipeptides, so this step fails.
Emulsification depends on bile salts, maltase is already active in intestinal juice, and pepsin is activated by HCl in the stomach. None of these needs enterokinase.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 16 · Digestion and Absorption

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List-I (cell type) with List-II (secretion) and choose the correct option.
List-I:
A. Oxyntic cells
B. Peptic cells
C. Goblet cells
D. Hepatocytes
List-II:
i. Bile
ii. Mucus
iii. Pepsinogen
iv. HCl and intrinsic factor
questions.explanation:
A-iv: Oxyntic (parietal) cells of the gastric glands secrete HCl and intrinsic factor.
B-iii: Peptic (chief) cells secrete the proenzyme pepsinogen.
C-ii: Goblet cells of the mucosal epithelium secrete mucus, which lubricates and protects the lining.
D-i: Liver cells (hepatocytes) secrete bile, which is stored in the gall bladder.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 16 · Digestion and Absorption

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which cells of the gastric glands secrete the proenzyme pepsinogen?
options: Goblet cells of the intestinal mucosa
questions.explanation:
Gastric glands contain three major cell types.
Mucus neck cells secrete mucus.
Peptic (chief) cells secrete pepsinogen, which is the inactive proenzyme.
Oxyntic (parietal) cells secrete HCl and Castle's intrinsic factor, not pepsinogen.
Goblet cells secrete mucus, and they are not part of the gastric glands.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 16 · Digestion and Absorption

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
In a person, an autoimmune disorder destroys most of the oxyntic (parietal) cells of the gastric glands, while the other gastric cells remain normal. Which set of consequences is most likely?
(i) Gastric pH rises well above 1.8.
(ii) Conversion of pepsinogen to pepsin is impaired.
(iii) Absorption of vitamin $B_{12}$ is reduced.
(iv) Secretion of pepsinogen stops completely.
questions.explanation:
Oxyntic cells secrete HCl and Castle's intrinsic factor.
(i) Likely: less HCl means the gastric pH rises above 1.8.
(ii) Likely: HCl is needed to convert pepsinogen to pepsin, so activation is impaired.
(iii) Likely: intrinsic factor is essential for vitamin $B_{12}$ absorption, so absorption falls.
(iv) Unlikely: pepsinogen comes from the peptic (chief) cells, which are unaffected.
So (i), (ii) and (iii) are the expected consequences.
Answer: (4)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 16 · Digestion and Absorption

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Statement I: In the muscularis of the alimentary canal, the smooth muscle is usually arranged as an inner longitudinal layer and an outer circular layer.
Statement II: An additional oblique muscle layer may be present in some regions of the alimentary canal.
Choose the correct option.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation:
Statement I is incorrect. The usual arrangement is the reverse: an inner circular layer and an outer longitudinal layer.
Statement II is correct. NCERT states that an oblique muscle layer may be present in some regions.
Answer: (4)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 16 · Digestion and Absorption

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List-I (substance absorbed) with List-II (mechanism of absorption).
List-I
A. Fructose
B. $Na^+$ ions
C. Water
D. Fatty acids and glycerol
List-II
(i) Depends on the osmotic gradient
(ii) Active transport against a concentration gradient
(iii) Carrier-mediated facilitated transport
(iv) Incorporated into micelles, re-formed as chylomicrons and passed into lacteals
questions.explanation:
A-iii: Fructose is absorbed by facilitated (carrier-mediated) transport.
B-ii: Electrolytes such as $Na^+$ are absorbed by active transport.
C-i: Water moves according to the osmotic gradient.
D-iv: Fatty acids and glycerol are insoluble. They enter micelles, are re-formed into chylomicrons in the mucosa, and pass into lacteals.
Answer: (4)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 16 · Digestion and Absorption

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In the muscularis layer of the human alimentary canal, the smooth muscle fibres are usually arranged as:
options: An inner longitudinal layer and an outer circular layer
An inner circular layer and an outer longitudinal layer
A single oblique layer throughout the canal
Striated muscle bundles arranged at random
questions.explanation:
The muscularis is made of smooth muscle. It is usually arranged as an inner circular layer and an outer longitudinal layer.
An oblique muscle layer may also be present, but only in some regions, such as the stomach.
Option (1) is tempting, but it reverses the order of the two layers.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 16 · Digestion and Absorption

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The oesophagus opens into which part of the stomach?
questions.explanation:
The stomach has three major parts: cardiac, fundic and pyloric.
The oesophagus opens into the cardiac portion.
The pyloric portion is the part that opens into the duodenum, the first part of the small intestine.
There is no 'duodenal portion' of the stomach.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 16 · Digestion and Absorption

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Assertion (A): Bile plays an important role in the digestion of fats even though it is secreted into the duodenum along with pancreatic juice.
Reason (R): Bile contains the enzyme lipase, which breaks fats into fatty acids and glycerol.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true. Bile salts emulsify fats into very small micelles, which increases the surface area for lipase. Bile also activates lipases.
R is false. Bile contains bile pigments (bilirubin, biliverdin), bile salts, cholesterol and phospholipids, but no enzymes. Lipase comes from pancreatic juice and intestinal juice.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 16 · Digestion and Absorption

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Statement I: Serosa is the innermost layer of the wall of the alimentary canal, lining its lumen.
Statement II: The mucosa forms irregular folds called rugae in the stomach and small finger-like projections called villi in the small intestine.
Choose the correct option.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation:
Statement I is incorrect. Serosa is the outermost layer, made of mesothelium with some connective tissue.
The mucosa is the innermost layer that lines the lumen. The layers from outside to inside are serosa, muscularis, sub-mucosa and mucosa.
Statement II is correct. The mucosa forms rugae in the stomach and villi in the small intestine.
Answer: (4)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 16 · Digestion and Absorption

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In the small intestine, the inactive enzyme trypsinogen is converted into active trypsin by enterokinase. Enterokinase is secreted by:
questions.explanation:
Pancreatic juice carries trypsinogen in an inactive form.
Enterokinase, secreted by the intestinal mucosa, converts trypsinogen into active trypsin.
The pancreas secretes trypsinogen itself, not the activator, so option (1) is the tempting trap.
Chief cells secrete pepsinogen, and liver cells produce bile, which has no enzymes.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 16 · Digestion and Absorption

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following are components of pancreatic juice?
Trypsinogen, chymotrypsinogen, procarboxypeptidases, amylases, nucleases, enterokinase, pepsinogen, maltase
questions.explanation:
Present in pancreatic juice: trypsinogen, chymotrypsinogen, procarboxypeptidases, amylases and nucleases. That makes 5. Pancreatic juice also contains lipases.
Not present:
- Enterokinase is secreted by the intestinal mucosa; it activates trypsinogen.
- Pepsinogen comes from the peptic cells of the gastric glands.
- Maltase is an enzyme of succus entericus (intestinal juice).
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 16 · Digestion and Absorption

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List-I (site of absorption) with List-II (substances absorbed):
List-I
A. Mouth
B. Stomach
C. Small intestine
D. Large intestine
List-II
(i) Water, some minerals and drugs
(ii) Certain drugs through the mucosa and lower side of the tongue
(iii) Principal site; glucose, fructose, amino acids, fatty acids and glycerol
(iv) Water, simple sugars and alcohol
questions.explanation:
A-(ii): In the mouth, certain drugs are absorbed into capillaries of the mucosa and the lower side of the tongue.
B-(iv): The stomach absorbs water, simple sugars and alcohol.
C-(iii): The small intestine is the principal organ of absorption for the final digestion products.
D-(i): The large intestine absorbs water, some minerals and drugs.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 16 · Digestion and Absorption

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The outermost layer of the wall of the human alimentary canal is the serosa. It is made up of:
options: Smooth muscle fibres arranged in circular and longitudinal layers
A thin mesothelium with some connective tissue
Loose connective tissue with nerves, blood and lymph vessels
questions.explanation:
The gut wall from oesophagus to rectum has four layers. From the outside in, they are serosa, muscularis, submucosa and mucosa.
The serosa is the outermost layer. It is a thin mesothelium, the epithelium covering visceral organs, with some connective tissue.
Option (1) describes the muscularis. Option (3) describes the submucosa. Option (4) describes the mucosa.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 16 · Digestion and Absorption

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The human stomach is best described as a:
options: U-shaped tube in the lower right abdominal cavity
J-shaped bag-like structure in the upper left portion of the abdominal cavity
J-shaped bag-like structure in the lower left portion of the abdominal cavity
Coiled tube in the upper right portion of the abdominal cavity
questions.explanation:
The oesophagus leads into a J-shaped, bag-like stomach.
The stomach lies in the upper left portion of the abdominal cavity.
The U-shaped structure that emerges from the stomach is the duodenum, so option (1) describes the wrong organ.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 16 · Digestion and Absorption

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In humans, each tooth is embedded in a socket of the jaw bone. This type of tooth attachment is described as:
questions.explanation:
NCERT describes human teeth as thecodont because each tooth sits in a socket of the jaw bone.
Diphyodont refers to having two successive sets of teeth (milk and permanent).
Heterodont refers to having different types of teeth.
Homodont means all teeth are alike, which does not apply to humans.
Only 'thecodont' describes the mode of attachment.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 16 · Digestion and Absorption

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following are absorbed into the blood by active transport, according to NCERT?
Glucose, amino acids, $Na^+$, water, fatty acids, glycerol
questions.explanation:
Glucose: active transport, a monosaccharide moved against the gradient.
Amino acids: active transport.
$Na^+$: an electrolyte absorbed by active transport.
Water: not active; it moves along the osmotic gradient.
Fatty acids and glycerol: not active; they are insoluble, enter as micelles and are carried in lymph as chylomicrons.
Total = 3.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 16 · Digestion and Absorption

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The urge to remove faeces stored in the rectum is initiated by
options: the hormone secretin released from the duodenal mucosa
a neural reflex triggered by the presence of faeces in the rectum
cholecystokinin acting on the rectal muscles
gastric inhibitory peptide acting on the anal sphincters
questions.explanation:
Faeces are stored temporarily in the rectum.
Their presence in the rectum initiates a neural reflex, and this reflex causes the urge for removal.
The trigger is neural, not hormonal.
Secretin, CCK and GIP are gastrointestinal hormones that regulate digestive secretions and gastric activity. None of them initiates defaecation.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 16 · Digestion and Absorption

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A patient has most of the stomach mucosa surgically removed. Months later, he develops symptoms of vitamin $B_{12}$ deficiency, even though his diet contains enough of the vitamin. Loss of which gastric secretion best explains this?
options: Pepsinogen from peptic cells, because $B_{12}$ is released only after protein digestion
Mucus from neck cells, because $B_{12}$ is absorbed only through mucus
Rennin, because it is needed to absorb all vitamins
Intrinsic factor from oxyntic cells, which is essential for absorbing vitamin $B_{12}$
questions.explanation:
The patient's diet supplies enough $B_{12}$, so the problem must be with absorption.
Oxyntic (parietal) cells secrete Castle's intrinsic factor, which is essential for absorbing vitamin $B_{12}$.
Removing the gastric mucosa removes these cells, so $B_{12}$ is not absorbed.
Pepsinogen loss reduces protein digestion in the stomach but does not stop $B_{12}$ absorption.
Rennin is an infant milk-protein enzyme.
Answer: (4)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 16 · Digestion and Absorption

questions.subject: Biology
questions.explanation:
Feature (1) describes villi with microvilli (the brush border). Villi are found in the small intestine, which rules out the stomach, oesophagus and colon.
Feature (2) describes the crypts of Lieberkuhn, which also point to the small intestine.
Feature (3) describes glands in the sub-mucosa. According to NCERT, glands are present in the sub-mucosa of the duodenum.
The stomach is a tempting choice because it has glands, but its gastric glands are mucosal, and its mucosa forms rugae, not villi.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 16 · Digestion and Absorption

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following are parts of the human large intestine?
Caecum, Jejunum, Transverse colon, Rectum, Duodenum, Descending colon
questions.explanation:
The large intestine consists of the caecum, the colon (ascending, transverse and descending parts) and the rectum.
Caecum: part of the large intestine.
Transverse colon: part of the large intestine.
Descending colon: part of the large intestine.
Rectum: part of the large intestine.
Jejunum and duodenum: both are regions of the small intestine.
That makes 4 parts of the large intestine.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 16 · Digestion and Absorption

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Mucus and bicarbonates provide a suitable medium for enzymatic action in the small intestine. The approximate pH of this medium is
questions.explanation:
Goblet cells secrete mucus, and the pancreas supplies bicarbonates.
Together they protect the intestinal mucosa from the acidic chyme and create an alkaline medium of pH 7.8.
pH 1.8 is close to the acidic pH of the stomach, so option (1) is wrong.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 16 · Digestion and Absorption

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following are present in pancreatic juice?
Trypsinogen, Chymotrypsinogen, Maltase, Nucleases, Enterokinase, Amylase, Dipeptidases, Lipases
questions.explanation:
Pancreatic juice contains trypsinogen, chymotrypsinogen, procarboxypeptidases, amylases, lipases and nucleases.
From the list, the pancreatic ones are trypsinogen, chymotrypsinogen, nucleases, amylase and lipases. That makes 5.
Maltase and dipeptidases belong to succus entericus.
Enterokinase is secreted by the intestinal mucosa.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 16 · Digestion and Absorption

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II.
List-I
A. Glottis
B. Epiglottis
C. Gastro-oesophageal sphincter
D. Pyloric sphincter
List-II
i. Guards the opening of the stomach into the duodenum
ii. Opening of the wind pipe
iii. Regulates the opening of the oesophagus into the stomach
iv. Cartilaginous flap
Choose the correct option.
questions.explanation:
A-ii: The glottis is the opening of the wind pipe.
B-iv: The epiglottis is a cartilaginous flap that covers the glottis.
C-iii: The gastro-oesophageal sphincter regulates the opening of the oesophagus into the stomach.
D-i: The pyloric sphincter guards the opening of the stomach into the duodenum.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 16 · Digestion and Absorption

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Assertion (A): Under the microscope, the free surface of the cells lining the intestinal villi looks like a brush.
Reason (R): These cells carry numerous microvilli, which greatly increase the absorptive surface area.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true. The epithelial cells lining the villi show a brush border appearance.
R is true. These cells have numerous microvilli, and these modifications increase the surface area enormously.
The brush border is simply the microvilli seen together. So R correctly explains A.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 16 · Digestion and Absorption

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following statements regarding carbohydrate digestion are correct?
(i) Salivary amylase hydrolyses about 30% of starch into maltose at an optimum pH of 6.8.
(ii) Pancreatic amylase converts polysaccharides into disaccharides.
(iii) Sucrase converts sucrose into glucose and fructose.
(iv) Lactase converts lactose into glucose and galactose.
(v) Maltase converts maltose into glucose and fructose.
questions.explanation:
(i) Correct: salivary amylase hydrolyses about 30% of starch to maltose at pH 6.8.
(ii) Correct: pancreatic amylase digests polysaccharides to disaccharides.
(iii) Correct: sucrase splits sucrose into glucose and fructose.
(iv) Correct: lactase splits lactose into glucose and galactose.
(v) Incorrect: maltase splits maltose into two glucose molecules, not glucose and fructose.
So 4 statements are correct.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 16 · Digestion and Absorption

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Statement I: Every papilla on the upper surface of the human tongue bears taste buds.
Statement II: The tongue is a freely movable muscular organ of the oral cavity.
Choose the correct option.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation:
Statement I is incorrect. NCERT says the upper surface of the tongue has small projections called papillae, and only some of them bear taste buds, not every one.
Statement II is correct. The tongue is described as a freely movable muscular organ attached to the floor of the oral cavity by the frenulum.
Answer: (4)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 16 · Digestion and Absorption

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List-I (disorder) with List-II (feature):
List-I
A. Jaundice
B. Vomiting
C. Diarrhoea
D. Constipation
List-II
(i) Reflex controlled by the medulla
(ii) Faeces retained in rectum due to irregular bowel movements
(iii) Deposition of bile pigments in skin and eyes
(iv) Reduced absorption of food
questions.explanation:
A-(iii): in jaundice, bile pigments are deposited in the skin and eyes, turning them yellow.
B-(i): vomiting is a reflex controlled by the vomit centre in the medulla.
C-(iv): diarrhoea reduces the absorption of food.
D-(ii): in constipation, faeces are retained in the rectum due to irregular bowel movements.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 16 · Digestion and Absorption

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The large intestine of humans consists of:
options: Colon, rectum and anal canal only, without the caecum
questions.explanation:
NCERT states that the ileum opens into the large intestine, which consists of the caecum, colon and rectum.
The duodenum, jejunum and ileum together form the small intestine.
The ileum therefore cannot be part of the large intestine.
The caecum is the first part of the large intestine, so it cannot be left out.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 16 · Digestion and Absorption

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Suppose a person's intestinal mucosa fails to secrete enterokinase, while all other secretions are normal. Which of the following would most directly result?
options: Starch digestion in the small intestine stops completely because pancreatic amylase remains inactive
Protein digestion in the small intestine is severely reduced, because trypsin is not formed and so chymotrypsin and carboxypeptidase are also not activated
Emulsification of fats in the duodenum stops because bile salts are not activated
Pepsin activity in the stomach ceases because pepsinogen cannot be converted to pepsin
questions.explanation:
Enterokinase, secreted by the intestinal mucosa, converts trypsinogen into trypsin.
Trypsin then activates chymotrypsinogen and procarboxypeptidase. Without enterokinase, none of these three proteases becomes active, so protein digestion in the intestine suffers badly.
(1) is wrong because pancreatic amylase is secreted in active form.
(3) is wrong because bile emulsifies fats without any enterokinase.
(4) is wrong because pepsinogen in the stomach is activated by HCl.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 16 · Digestion and Absorption

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The vermiform appendix, a narrow finger-like vestigial projection in humans, arises from which part of the alimentary canal?
questions.explanation:
NCERT describes the caecum as a small blind sac of the large intestine that hosts some symbiotic micro-organisms.
The vermiform appendix is a narrow, finger-like tubular projection that arises from the caecum. It is vestigial in humans.
The ileum opens into the caecum but does not give rise to the appendix.
The ascending colon comes after the caecum, so it is not the origin either.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 16 · Digestion and Absorption

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which one of the following statements about the human intestine is INCORRECT?
options: Brunner's glands are present in the submucosa of the duodenum
The small intestinal mucosa forms finger-like folds called villi, which increase the absorptive surface
The hepato-pancreatic duct opens into the ileum and is guarded by the sphincter of Oddi
The caecum is a blind sac from which a vestigial projection, the vermiform appendix, arises
questions.explanation:
(1) Correct: NCERT places Brunner's glands in the duodenal submucosa.
(2) Correct: villi in the small intestine greatly increase the surface area for absorption.
(3) Incorrect: the common hepato-pancreatic duct opens into the duodenum, not the ileum. The sphincter of Oddi does guard this opening, which makes the statement look tempting.
(4) Correct: the appendix arises from the blind caecum.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 16 · Digestion and Absorption

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about sites of absorption in the human alimentary canal is INCORRECT?
options: Certain drugs in contact with the mucosa of the mouth and lower side of the tongue are absorbed into blood capillaries
Water, simple sugars and alcohol are absorbed in the stomach
The large intestine absorbs water, some minerals and some drugs
The large intestine is the principal site for absorption of amino acids and monosaccharides
questions.explanation:
(1) Correct: some drugs are absorbed through the mucosa of the mouth and the lower side of the tongue.
(2) Correct: the stomach absorbs water, simple sugars and alcohol.
(3) Correct: the large intestine absorbs water, some minerals and drugs.
(4) Incorrect: the small intestine is the principal organ for absorbing digested nutrients such as amino acids and monosaccharides. The large intestine does not have this role.
Answer: (4)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 16 · Digestion and Absorption

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match the two columns and select the correct among options given
Column I: A. Biomacromolecules of food; B. Human digestive system; C. Stomach; D. Thecodont; E. Serosa
Column II: i. Alimentary canal and associated gland; ii. Embedded in jawbones; iii. Outer wall of visceral organs; iv. Converted into simple substances; v. J-shaped bag like structure
questions.explanation:
A–iv: food biomacromolecules are converted into simple, absorbable substances.
B–i: the human digestive system consists of the alimentary canal and associated glands.
C–v: the stomach is a J-shaped, bag-like structure.
D–ii: thecodont teeth are embedded in sockets of the jawbones.
E–iii: serosa is the outermost layer of the wall of visceral organs.
This sequence (iv, i, v, ii, iii) matches option (2).
Answer: (2)
questions.credit: Source: NCERT Exemplar Biology Class 11, Ch 16 (MCQ Q5)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 16 · Digestion and Absorption

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II.
List-I
(A) Thecodont
(B) Diphyodont
(C) Heterodont
(D) Papillae
List-II
(i) Teeth of different types in the same jaw
(ii) Small projections on the upper surface of the tongue
(iii) Teeth embedded in sockets of jaw bones
(iv) Two sets of teeth formed during life
Choose the correct option.
questions.explanation:
(A) Thecodont means each tooth is set in a jaw-bone socket, so A-iii.
(B) Diphyodont means milk teeth are replaced by permanent teeth, giving two sets, so B-iv.
(C) Heterodont means four kinds of teeth: incisors, canines, premolars and molars, so C-i.
(D) Papillae are projections on the dorsal surface of the tongue, so D-ii.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 16 · Digestion and Absorption

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Arrange the following events in fat digestion and absorption in the correct order:
